items.q: Do I need a YouTube or Google account?
items.a: No. Playback runs through the public YouTube IFrame player. There's no sign-in anywhere in LoopTV.

items.q: Where does the catalog come from?
items.a: A twice-monthly GitHub workflow refreshes public channel metadata through a cache-first YouTube Data API path, with yt-dlp as a fallback. It commits a checked-in catalog.json, so watching needs no runtime API key; refresh credentials stay in repository Actions.

items.q: What happens when a video can't be embedded?
items.a: YouTube returns error 101 or 150 when a channel blocks embedding for a specific clip. The player catches it and immediately picks the next random video — no error toast, no interruption.

items.q: Where is my watch history stored?
items.a: Entirely in your browser's localStorage. Clearing site data wipes it. There is no server-side account or database.

items.q: Can I add my own channels?
items.a: Yes — LoopTV is MIT-licensed. Fork the repo, append a station to stations.json, run pnpm run build:catalog (requires yt-dlp), and deploy.
